summary: vanexa-agent daemon executes remote-driven shell/tool commands via author-controlled Cloudflare Workers relay
details: The `vanexa-agent start` daemon opens a WebSocket and dispatches `tool_call` messages received over that channel into `child_process.spawn` / `execSync` and filesystem/network tool handlers, giving whoever controls the paired remote endpoint arbitrary shell execution on the installer's host. The transport is not the LAN-only WebSocket described in the README: the bundle hardcodes two personal Cloudflare Workers subdomains, `vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev` and `vanexa-ai-proxy.hanazaki542.workers.dev`, and routes command traffic, session state read from `~/.vanexa/session.jwt`, config from `~/.vanexa/config.json`, and BYOK LLM API keys through them. The operator of those Workers sees all command traffic and LLM prompts/keys and can inject `tool_call` payloads that the local agent will execute against the host's shell and filesystem. This is a network-source-to-shell-sink code path (backdoor) whose blast radius is expanded by an undisclosed author-controlled relay standing between the operator and the tool loop.
